									Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images
	

		
	
				
	On the opening night of his 30-concert residency at Madison Square Garden, pop superstar Harry Styles paid tribute to the late, great Dolly Parton. And at the tail end of Saturday night’s show, he shouted-out his ex-girlfriend Taylor Swift’s wedding to Travis Kelce.


	“We’re at Madison Square Garden, home of the world champion New York Knicks!” Styles announced to loud applause, before adding, “And they also do weddings.”
	

	Styles famously dated Swift from November 2012 to January 2013 and served as the inspiration for Swift’s chart-topping 2014 song “Style.” According to Variety, Styles even “received an invitation” to Swift’s wedding to NFL star Travis Kelce on July 3 at Madison Square Garden, but sources said that “Styles is currently on tour and will not make it to MSG.” However, Styles’ fiancé, Zoe Kravitz, did end up attending the Swift-Kelce mega-wedding. 


	There appears to be no bad blood between the two exes. Styles even gave a cheeky nod to Swift’s wedding during his record-breaking Wembley residency on July 3, performing his 2017 song “Two Ghosts,” which is believed to be his response to her tune “Style,” as he sings: “Same lips red, same eyes blue / Same white shirt, couple more tattoos.”


	
		More from Variety

title: Owner of ‘Heated Rivalry’ Cabin Needed to Do Some ‘Soul Searching’ Before Inviting the Show Back for Season 2
description: Michael Kutryk, the owner of the now-famous cabin featured in “Heated Rivalry” Season 1, said he needed to do some “soul searching” before allowing
body:
Michael Kutryk, the owner of the now-famous cabin featured in “Heated Rivalry” Season 1, said he needed to do some “soul searching” before allowing the HBO production to come back for Season 2.

	“I did a little bit of soul searching about allowing them to come back,” Kutryk told HGTV. “I know they need it, and I realize I [could] be difficult and try to squeeze them, but I [couldn’t] bring myself to do that.”


	He continued, “When they called, they said, ‘How much do you want?’ First, I told them they scratched my table, then I named a very reasonable price. They were shocked and appreciative. I actually didn’t even get them to replace my table.”
	

	Kutryk’s house was featured in the “Heated Rivalry” Season 1 finale, titled “The Cottage,” in which Shane Hollander (Hudson Williams) brings Ilya Rozanov (Connor Storrie) to his remote family cabin for a private getaway. Kutryk, a Toronto doctor, said he was shocked when he first listened to Rachel Reid’s “Game Changer,” on which the show is based, on audiobook.

	“My jaw just dropped as I listened. The pretty explicit nature of the book made me wonder just what they’d be filming … and showing!” Kutryk said. “I just thought, OK, they’re gonna film what they’re gonna film. What’s done is done.”

	“We’ll see after Season 2 airs what demand is like,” he added. “It’s still true: I’m a private guy. This is my retreat. I built this to get away from the world, so I don’t know how much longer I’ll continue to share it.”

	“Heated Rivalry” Season 2, which was greenlit in December 2025, is expected to release in April 2027. The HBO Max and Crave series follows up-and-coming professional hockey stars Shane Hollander and Ilya Rozanov, who maintain a facade as fierce competitors on the ice while engaging in a secret romance.

title: Chris Hansen Says Robert Pattinson’s ‘Primetime’ Performance Is ‘Overly Dramatic,’ But His Wife and Kids Think It’s a ‘Pretty Good Imitation’

body:
Chris Hansen recently gave his reaction to Robert Pattinson’s impression of him in the upcoming A24 drama-thriller “Primetime,” which chronicles Hansen’s stint as host of Dateline NBC’s “To Catch a Predator.”

	“I mean, obviously he has practiced imitating me, and while I think it’s overly dramatic, I think there is a pretty good imitation there in the trailer,” Hansen told Entertainment Tonight. “It’s not so much what I think; it’s what other people think. And you know, my wife [and] my family seem to think it’s a pretty good imitation.”
	

	“He’s saying things I never said and doing things I never did, and that’s not who I am. I’m a nice guy, except when it comes to criminals and predators,” he added. “I think people should remember that it is a work of fiction, only based on real-life events.”


	Reps for Pattinson did not immediately respond to a request for comment regarding Hansen’s comments. 

	Hansen recently told Fox News’ “Jesse Watters Primetime” that when he showed up at the A24 offices for a private screening of the film, he was asked to sign a legal agreement that would sign away several of his personal rights.

	“The lawyers at A24 wanted me to sign away my rights to my name, image and brand, essentially, as well as any potential legal rights that would come out of the movie,” Hansen claimed. “I couldn’t sign that, so they didn’t show me the film. I went all the way over there.”

	A source close to A24 said at the time that Hansen was asked to sign an NDA that every preview audience must adhere to for an unreleased project.

title: Box Office: ‘The Dog Stars’ Struggles With Just $3 Million on Friday; ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ to Win Weekend Again
description: 20th Century’s “The Dog Stars” and Keylight Pictures’ “Coyote vs. Acme” both debuted in theaters on Friday, but Sony and Marvel’s “Spider-Man: Brand
body:
20th Century’s “The Dog Stars” and Keylight Pictures’ “Coyote vs. Acme” both debuted in theaters on Friday, but Sony and Marvel’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” will once again win the weekend.

	“Coyote vs. Acme” fared best of the two major newcomers, landing in second place with an estimated $5.2 million domestically on Friday from 3,575 screens. The “Looney Tunes” live-action animation hybrid comedy should gross about $13.5 million by Sunday
	

	From director Dave Green, “Coyote vs. Acme” puts a twist on the classic Road Runner cartoons. After Acme products (think anvils and rocket skates) failed him one too many times, Wile E. Coyote takes the ubiquitous gadget manufacturer to court. Will Forte and Lana Condor star alongside John Cena, Tone Bell, Martha Kelly, Luis Guzmán, P.J. Byrne and John Early.


	“The Dog Stars” fell to No. 4 after earning just $3 million on Friday from 3,330 North American theaters. Rival estimates have the Ridley Scott action drama making $7.2 million through the weekend. 

	Jacob Elordi leads “The Dog Stars” as a lonely man with a canine companion living in a post-apocalyptic wasteland. When he discovers a mysterious transmission, he is determined to find its source. Other cast members include Margaret Qualley, Josh Brolin, Guy Pearce, Allison Janney and Benedict Wong.

	“Spider-Man: Brand New Day” is still leading the domestic box office through its fifth weekend in theaters. It added $5.5 million on Friday and should pull in $21 million by Sunday. That would notch the North American total for Sony-Marvel superhero epic to $890 million.
	

	Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” continues to show out as it enters its seventh weekend, taking third with $3.7 million on Friday. By the end of the weekend, the sprawling historical drama should earn $14.6 million, pushing its domestic haul to $564 million.

	“Insidious: Out of the Further” made $2.9 million on Friday, slotting at No. 5. By the end of its sophomore weekend, it’s expected to make $9.32 million, which represents about a 60% drop from last week’s debut. $9.32 million would bring the horror sequel’s North American revenues to about $42.85 million.

body:
Ray Winstone recently recalled to The Times of London that he once told off an unnamed director after he saw them “groping” his female co-star.

	“I had this director once,” Winstone said. “I was in a scene where I had to pick up this girl, and the director wanted to show me what to do. But he was groping her. That was it. I said, ‘Don’t you dare do that.’ He abused his power, took advantage, and she was a good kid, you know, who seemed a little lost. Anyway, it was dealt with.”
	

	When asked in what matter the situation was “dealt with,” Winstone added, “Well, back in the day, if there was a wrong ’un on set, 99 times out of 100 it was sorted, either by the hairy-arse riggers or sparks. I’ve done it myself too, taken someone to the side to give them a slap or to tell them, in no uncertain terms, to behave. But it’s a different world today.”


	Winstone will soon star in Season 2 of “The Gentlemen,” which recently got the green light for its third season on Netflix. In the Guy Ritchie crime drama, Winstone plays kingpin Bobby Glass. Later in his sit-down with The Times, he said the role made him realize he is “getting old.”

	“When you’re not the young lead but the old boy, who everyone says they’ve got to look after because he’s getting on a bit,” Winstone said. The Times then asked if he had any plans to slow down his career, and Winstone quipped, “Well, you’ve got to pay the taxman, haven’t you?”

title: Venice Film Festival Jury Press Conference ‘Probably Not’ Happening Due to Scheduling, Will Replace Event With Welcome Cocktails for Journalists
description:

	The festival, which kicks off Sept. 2 wi
body:
The Venice Film Festival is weighing scrapping its traditional opening jury press conference on the Lido.

	The festival, which kicks off Sept. 2 with the world premiere of Danny Boyle’s “Ink,” told Variety that the presser will “probably not” take place, citing a scheduling conflict, and said a welcome cocktail hour with the press will be organized instead. If the press conference is axed, it could raise eyebrows given the political pressure building around Venice this year.
	

	Last year’s Venice opening jury press conference was dominated by questions about Gaza, with then-jury president Alexander Payne saying he felt “unprepared” to answer a question about the conflict and was blamed for seemingly dodging it.


	The news comes just days after Nobel Prize-winning author Annie Ernaux, Pink Floyd co-founder Roger Waters and filmmakers including Matteo Garrone and Isabel Coixet signed an open letter urging the Venice Biennale and film festival to take “concrete action in support of Palestine.” The letter was organized by the Venice4Palestine collective, which similarly targeted the festival last year and had urged the event’s organizers to withdraw invitations to Gerard Butler and Gal Gadot over their previous support for Israel.

	Venice artistic director Alberto Barbera has described this year’s lineup as Venice’s “most political” in recent years, with films tackling war, Palestine, immigration, climate change and shrinking political freedoms. Earlier this week, the fest added “NAZA,” a new hot-button documentary from “No Other Land” directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, to the Venice competition lineup.
	

	The festival’s main competition jury is headed by Maggie Gyllenhaal and includes Tunisian filmmaker Kaouther Ben Hania, whose acclaimed “The Voice of Hind Rajab,” about the killing of a five-year-old Palestinian girl in Gaza, premiered at Venice last year and won the Silver Lion Grand Jury Prize. Other jurors are Daniel Blumberg, Francesco Casetti, Xavier Giannoli, Shahrbanoo Sadat and Johnnie To.

title: Anne Hathaway Joins Tom Cruise in ‘Days of Thunder’ Follow-Up; Paramount Sets Release Date (EXCLUSIVE)

	Paramount Pictures has date
body:
Anne Hathaway will star opposite Tom Cruise in the next chapter of “Days of Thunder,” Variety has learned exclusively.

	Paramount Pictures has dated the feature film sequel for June 2, 2028, when Cruise and Hathaway will hit the road almost 40 years after the original Tony Scott film was released. The project will be shot for IMAX screens, and released exclusively in theaters for formats including Dolby Cinema and 4DX. Cruise released a promotional image on Saturday celebrating Hathaway’s casting and posing with his co-lead on a NASCAR track. 
	

	Cruise will reprise his role as the scrappy driver Cole Trickle. Plot details are scarce, but Hathaway is set to play a racecar team owner and engineer. Jonathan Levine (“Long Shot,” “Mr. Irrelevant”) is confirmed to direct. Cruise is producing alongside Jerry Bruckheimer and Tommy Harper. 


	In the original, Cruise’s Trickle gets recruited to a new NASCAR team by a retired racing legend (Robert Duvall). The first film also starred Nicole Kidman, Randy Quaid and John C. Reilly.

	Hathaway has been on a tear in 2026, with four films in theaters including “Mother Mary,” “The Devil Wears Prada 2,” “The Odyssey” and “The End of Oak Street.” The expecting movie star will close out the year with the Coleen Hoover adaptation “Verity.” She’s just wrapped production on the Adam Driver military drama “Alone at Dawn,” and is working on a three-quel to her star-making Disney movie “The Princess Diaries.” Hathaway is represented by CAA, Entertainment 360 and Apex Public Relations.
	

	The ”Days of Thunder” follow-up is the first significant piece of IP that Cruise will engage with after ramping down the “Mission: Impossible” franchise. He’s also on the hook for another “Top Gun” movie, and will return to the prestige drama space with this year’s Alejandro González Iñárritu film “Digger.”

title: ‘Borges and Me’ Review: Gentle, Nostalgic Literary Road Movie Is More Perky Than Poetic
description: American author Jay Parini’s 2020 memoir “Borges and Me: An Encounter” read as a charming extension of an anecdote any writer would dine out on for
body:
American author Jay Parini’s 2020 memoir “Borges and Me: An Encounter” read as a charming extension of an anecdote any writer would dine out on for the rest of their life: the tale of how Parini, as a college student in the 1970s, was somehow partnered on a winding road trip through the Scottish Highlands with the venerable Argentine literary icon José Luis Borges. Like any good anecdote, it feels healthily embellished — Borges was doubtless a character, but is fashioned on the page into a Character — in ways that director Marc Turtletaub‘s enjoyable, good-natured screen adaptation appears to build upon. As a feature film, “Borges and Me” is perhaps extended beyond its natural capacity: It feels both a tall story and a thin one. But the charm is still there.
	

	Benefiting considerably from the tawny, textured splendor of its Scottish locations — shot with dewy autumnal crispness by DP Christopher Norr — this is mellow, quietly sentimental fare that was ideally suited to its home-turf world premiere at the Edinburgh Film Festival. It will likely please plenty more crowds on the festival circuit en route to global arthouse-crossover distribution, assisted by the mixture of British, South American and North American drawcards in a transatlantic co-production. Those include its deliberately mismatched leads: Chilean veteran Luis Gnecco (“Neruda”) as the twinkly genius, and Fionn Whitehead (“Dunkirk”), an actor eternally English in his uprightness but appealingly cast an Anglophile American, as his exasperated minder.


	As played by White, the young Parini may be fairly advanced in his studies — as an English literature doctoral student at St. Andrew’s University in Scotland — but he exudes an unworldly freshman quality in his just-askew tortoiseshell glasses and oversized duffel coat. A native Pennsylvanian, and still very much a fish out of water, his shy, sweet earnestness makes him an easy target for good-humored ribbing by his breezily bohemian supervisor, the poet Alastair Reid (Alan Cumming, on pleasingly Alan Cumming form). A scholar of South American literature and a leading translator of Borges’ work, he invites the Chilean to stay with him at his ramshackle coastal cottage; joining them for a day, Parini is both bewildered and a little enraptured by the brilliant, eccentric and sightless septuagenarian visitor.
	

	He’s not, however, prepared to be Borges’ babysitter — which is precisely what he becomes when Reid heads off on a last-minute trip to London, leaving some pointers regarding the writer’s various medications, but not much else. It also happens to be the week when Parini was planning to drive up into the Highlands to interview his Ph.D subject, the elusive and hermetic poet George Mackay Brown (Peter Mullan, in a mischievous extended cameo). Cue a cross-generational odd-couple road trip, with rather more sightseeing detours than Parini had planned for. Borges may not be able to see the scenery, but delights in every scrap of local color, to a degree that the American — tasked with describing everything to his elder, in suitably lyrical terms — finds quite wearisome.

	Audiences might relate to some extent. In a sprightly performance rife with oddball mannerisms, Gnecco gives Borges equal parts impish wisdom, earthy vulgarity and childlike wonder, rarely letting a moment’s silence go unfilled with eager chatter. When the virginal Parini — who thus far has read romantic poetry without truly feeling it — hits it off with smart, kindly pub worker Ailith (a wonderful Freya Mavor) and they steal away for a time, the film positively breathes in the old man’s absence. 

	Borges’ presence accounts for some amusing and even poignant adventures: a bumbling boat excursion on Loch Ness, or a fanciful, hallucinatory visit to a long grassed-over battlefield. But the film’s most affecting moments are its quietest ones, largely centered on Parini and his interior anxieties, which include his less academically-inclined brother’s travails as a soldier in Vietnam. Whitehead gives “Borges and Me” the stillness it needs to avoid feeling mawkish or shticky, but screenwriter Oren Moverman (working from an earlier adaptation by Parini and Ross Clarke) pivots between moments of graceful poetry and others of simpler feelgood sentiment. 

	The final balance slightly favors the latter: There’s little engagement with Borges’ own writing, for example, though audiences so inclined have the upcoming five-hour-plus documentary “Life of Jorge Luis Borges” for that. (Perhaps the two films’ eventual distributors could put their heads together and work out a complementary release strategy.) Full of warm feeling and fuzzy nostalgia for the porous, knowledge-gathering naïveté of youth, “Borges and Me” treats the author as a general, buoyant, heavily imagined spirit rather than a historical subject, and likably so.

title: ‘New Girl’ Reunion Is Not Happening: ‘There Are No Scripts,’ Says Creator Liz Meriwether
description:
“New Girl” isn’t coming back anytime soon.

	Despite recent claims by Max Greenfield, who played Schmidt on the hit Fox sitcom, that he has read “am
body:
“New Girl” isn’t coming back anytime soon.

	Despite recent claims by Max Greenfield, who played Schmidt on the hit Fox sitcom, that he has read “amazing” scripts for a reunion, show creator Liz Meriwether insists, “There are no scripts.”

	I caught up with Meriwether at the Season 1 finale screening of her latest hit series “Furious” on Thursday night at the DGA in West Hollywood.


	“I don’t even have the scripts written for the things that I need to have scripts written for,” said Meriwether, who is adapting Britney Spears’s memoir “The Woman in Me” for a movie to be directed by Jon M. Chu and produce by Marc Platt.
	


	Greenfield set off speculation about a “New Girl” reunion in late July when he said during an appearance on “Today with Jenna & Sheinelle,” “As far as I know, it’s happening. I’ve seen scripts, they’re amazing.”

	Meriwether responded to Greenfield’s claim with a very tongue-in-cheek video on Instagram. “Max told everybody that there’s amazing scripts of a ‘New Girl’ reunion that I’ve written. Um — and just an update on that — the scripts were pretty good until everybody just started giving me notes on every little thing,” she cracked, before listing changes all of the stars of the show requested.

	For now, Meriwether told me, “I’ve honestly been enjoying this thing, whatever this is, that’s like this back and forth between the cast and me, and I think this is the show and I feel like maybe in the world of the internet…maybe the show is just this, these little videos, maybe that’s the reunion. I don’t know.”
	

	“New Girl” ran for seven seasons from 2011 to 2018.

	Greenfield eventually clarified his remarks exclusively with Variety, joking that he was confused because a reunion of sorts is happening. The cast, including Zooey Deschanel, Jake Johnson, Lamorne Morris, Hannah Simone and Damon Wayans Jr., will reunite at the Chrysalis Butterfly Ball in Los Angeles on Oct. 10 to receive the Rising Phoenix Award. Greenfield serves as host of the gala.

	The Rising Phoenix Award will recognize the series’ theme of starting over and people who make starting over possible.


	As for the Spears biopic, Meriwether said she can’t say much because it’s too early in the process: “It’s really interesting because I haven’t written a movie in a long time, so that’s been part of the process is just trying to think in a two-hour story as opposed to like an eight-hour story, which is what I’ve been used to doing.”

	She has yet to meet the “…Baby One More Time” hitmaker. “I would love to,” Meriwether said.




	

					Scoot McNairy, Emmy Rossum, Quincy Tyler Bernstine and Liz Meriwether at the “Furious” Los Angeles special screening at the DGA Theater on Aug. 27 in Los Angeles.
									Variety via Getty Images

title: Final Emmy Predictions in 116 Categories: HBO Max Poised to Dominate With ‘The Pitt’ as ‘Widow’s Bay’ and ‘Hacks’ Chase Opposite All-Time Records

body:
Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predictions for the upcoming Oscars, Emmys, Grammys and Tony Awards ceremonies, curated by Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis. The prediction pages reflect the current standings in the race and do not reflect personal preferences for any individual contender. As other formal (and informal) polls suggest, competitions are fluid and subject to change in response to buzz and events. Predictions are updated every Thursday.
	Primetime Emmys Predictions Commentary All Categories (Updated: Aug. 29, 2026): “The tribe has spoken.” For the first time in a while, the Emmy race feels genuinely quite settled in the drama race, while the comedy field has a legitimate insurgent, and the limited series category is anyone’s to lose. The ceremony could be a nail-biter. HBO Max’s medical drama and last year’s reigning drama champion “The Pitt” turned a real-time gimmick into the network’s defining series of the year. Apple TV’s horror hit “Widow’s Bay” bulldozed its way into the comedy conversation. At the same time, Netflix’s anthology series “Beef” returned to the fold to take on HBO’s murder-mystery “DTF St. Louis.”
	If the final predictions hold, the same year “Hacks” set the all-time comedy nomination record with 24 — surpassing the 23-nom mark “The Studio” tied with “The Bear” just last year — the Katie Dippold-created horror gem “Widow’s Bay” is projected to win an astounding 15 Emmys, including outstanding comedy series. That would make it the most awarded comedy series in a single year, breaking the record “The Studio” set only last year with 13.
	So where does that leave “Hacks?” The fifth and final season of Jean Smart’s Deborah Vance is projected for a single win — a record-setting eighth acting Emmy for Smart — while losing everywhere else. But the margin is razor-thin, and it points at a not-so-great possible record that could be set. If Lisa Kudrow pulls off what many consider to be impossible and eeks out a lead comedy actress win for the final season of “The Comeback” — denying Smart in the one category “Hacks” is otherwise projected to take — and if the show is blanked across the Creative Arts categories as well, the beloved farewell would back into a brutal headline: the most Emmy losses in a single season in history, surpassing the 21 that “The Handmaid’s Tale” lost in 2021.
	That shouldn’t bum out HBO Max too much, because the network is still projected to dominate the nights overall. “The Pitt” is expected to grow on its freshman tally of five to as many as seven, repeating in drama series and for Noah Wyle, Katherine LaNasa and casting. 
	The limited race looks tighter — HBO’s “DTF St. Louis” is most notably in play — but the second season of Netflix’s anthology “Beef” should squeak it out with six wins, helped by projected acting victories for Oscar Isaac and Carey Mulligan.
	Thanks to a new “area award” format — voters now judge each nominee against an approval threshold rather than picking one winner — the variety series category can crown more than one show. That could hand a beloved farewell to Stephen Colbert, whose “Late Show” won its first Emmy only last year and signs off in 2026, while simultaneously delivering a long-denied first series trophy to Jimmy Kimmel after a year spent tangling with the president and the F.C.C. In this category, in this format, they don’t have to beat each other.
	In other variety categories: “The Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show Starring Bad Bunny” is expected to become the most-awarded Super Bowl halftime show in Emmy history, surpassing the 2022 Dr. Dre/Snoop Dogg/Eminem LVI show, which won three. It would also be the first Spanish-language program to win variety special (live) — and Bad Bunny’s first Emmy.
	In variety special (pre-recorded), Taylor Swift is expected to win her first competitive Emmy — as a producer of her Disney+ “Eras Tour” special — even as her other awards ambitions play out well beyond television. Her “Toy Story 5″ song “I Knew It, I Knew You” is an early Oscar hopeful in the best original song race, while her album, “The Life of a Showgirl” will be seeking Grammy Awards consideration this cycle. Swift has technically been an Emmy winner since 2015, when “AMEX Unstaged: Taylor Swift Experience” took the juried prize for original interactive program. But a pre-recorded win would be her first competitive Emmy, chipping the asterisk off an EGOT-aspiring résumé.
	While CBS’ “Survivor,” coming off its landmark 50th season, looked like it could finally win its first statue for competition program, Peacock’s “The Traitors” appears poised to edge it out, though it’s close.
	A handful of races remain in flux, which only adds pressure to an evening emceed by Emmy winner (and Variety cover star) Mariska Hargitay, likely to become the first person to hold Emmy wins for acting (thanks “Law and Order”) and documentary, if she wins either doc series or director for “My Mom Jayne.”
	The Creative Arts ceremonies honoring the artisans, plus the Governors Gala, take place Sept. 5-6. The 78th Primetime Emmy Awards air Sept. 14 on NBC.

            Milo looked none too thrilled in his mug shot ... and TMZ also broke the news Saturday that Milo had been deported back to the U.K. following his arrest.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Kanye, meanwhile, still hit the stage Friday night at the Superdome ... performing for 2.5 hours without once mentioning Milo's ICE detention.

description:
'Bachelor' Star Clayton Echard
                          Fake Twins Accuser Pleads Guilty
body:
'Bachelor' Star Clayton Echard
                          Fake Twins Accuser Pleads Guilty
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Former "Bachelor" star Clayton Echard is finally getting some vindication ... because the woman who falsely claimed she was pregnant with his twins has pleaded guilty to fraud.
      
    
            Laura Owens pleaded guilty Friday to four felonies tied to fake pregnancy claims involving Echard and another man, according to The Arizona Republic.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Owens admitted to two counts of fraudulent schemes and artifices, one count of perjury and one count of taking another person's identity.
      

            The saga began in 2023, when Owens claimed Echard got her pregnant with twins and filed a paternity case seeking child support.
      
    
            Clayton denied he was the father ... and Owens later said she'd suffered a miscarriage.
      
    
            But the case didn't end there ... a judge later found Owens repeatedly lied during the proceedings and referred the matter to prosecutors ... who accused her of fabricating evidence to back up her pregnancy claims.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Prosecutors say Clayton wasn't her only alleged target ... claiming Owens made similar false pregnancy claims involving another man she dated in 2021.
      
    
            Owens was ultimately hit with 14 felony charges ... but under her plea deal, prosecutors agreed to dismiss the remaining 10.
      
    
            She could still wind up behind bars ... one fraud count leaves sentencing up to the judge, while the other three call for probation.
      
    
            Owens is scheduled to be sentenced October 23.
